description: M1 assumption-check set: 28 questions across Power Grid Recharged, Root (Learning to Play), Azul, Dune: Imperium. Topics are common disputes; wording is ours, some deliberately sloppy like at the table (tag 'sloppy'). expected_pages are physical PDF pages (1-based). All answers verified against the owner's PDFs on 2026-11-21.

questions.question: My hybrid plant burns 2 coal or oil. How much can I store on it, and can I mix coal and oil on it?
questions.expected_verdict: Up to twice its requirement (4 resources) in any mix of coal and oil.
questions.source: Power Grid FAQ topic (BGG wiki https://rpggeek.com/wiki/page/Power_Grid_FAQ; page blocked to fetch, wording ours)
questions.expected_quote: may store at most twice as many resource tokens as it has resource symbols

questions.question: I already have 3 plants and just won a 4th in the auction. What happens to my plants and the coal sitting on them?
questions.expected_verdict: Scrap one of your other plants (never the one you just bought): you may only own 3 plants at any time. Resources on the scrapped plant may move to your remaining plants if they can store them; otherwise they go back to the supply, not the resource market.
questions.source: Common dispute (rules summaries surfaced by web search, e.g. https://gamerules.com/rules/power-grid/); wording ours
questions.notes: Fixed for Recharged: no 2-player 4-plant exception (2p uses the Trust variant); leftover resources go to the supply, not the market.
questions.expected_quote: each player may own only 3 power plants at any time

questions.question: First round — can I just pass on the auction and not buy a plant?
questions.expected_verdict: No. In the first round every player must buy a power plant.
questions.expected_quote: During the first round of the game each player must buy 1 power plant

questions.question: Early game: can I build a house in Berlin if my friend already has one there?
questions.expected_verdict: Not in Step 1: each city can only be connected by one player. In Step 2 two players can connect to a city, in Step 3 three (spaces cost 10, 15, 20 Elektro). A player may never connect to the same city twice.
questions.expected_quote: In Step 1 of the game, each city can only be connected by one player

questions.question: Game over and two of us powered the same number of cities. Who wins?
questions.expected_verdict: The tied player with the most Elektro (money) left wins.
questions.expected_quote: If there is a tie, the player with the most remaining money wins

questions.question: and if we also have exactly the same money?
questions.expected_verdict: Not covered: the rulebook only breaks a tie by most remaining money and gives no further tie-breaker. Treat it as a shared win or a house rule.
questions.notes: Fixed for Recharged: the rulebook has only one tie-breaker. Tests a follow-up that ends in Not covered.
questions.expected_quote: If there is a tie, the player with the most remaining money wins

questions.question: Can I lend 20 Elektro to another player and have them pay me back next round?
questions.expected_verdict: Not covered by the rulebook (no rules for loans or trading money between players); treat as a house-rule decision.
questions.notes: Verified: no rules about loans or giving money between players.

questions.question: do i gotta put a house down round one or can i chill and start later
questions.expected_verdict: You can wait: players do not have to choose their starting cities in the first round and may start their network in a later round.
questions.expected_quote: The players do not have to choose their starting cities in the first round

questions.question: I'm the attacker. Can I play an ambush card?
questions.expected_verdict: No. Only the defender may play an ambush card (matching the battle clearing, or a bird). The attacker may only play a matching ambush card to cancel the defender's ambush.
questions.source: Ambush questions on community Q&A surfaced by web search (Law excerpts, Steam discussion https://steamcommunity.com/app/965580/discussions/0/2952628008343000369); wording ours
questions.expected_quote: the defender may play an ambush card whose suit matches the clearing of battle

questions.question: The cats and I both have 2 pieces in a clearing. Who rules it?
questions.expected_verdict: Nobody rules it when tied — except the Eyrie, who rule tied clearings where they have pieces (Lords of the Forest).
questions.source: Rule/control questions surfaced by web search (https://lehi-innovation.github.io/boardgame-rules/rules/root/); wording ours
questions.notes: Verified. Eyrie exception "Lords of the Forest" is on p.12 (multi-page evidence).
questions.expected_quote: On a tie, no one is ruler

questions.question: can my guys walk from a spot the cats own to another spot the cats also own?
questions.expected_verdict: No. To move you must rule the clearing you move from or the clearing you move to.
questions.expected_quote: To move, you must rule the clearing you are moving from or moving to

questions.question: If I have to spend a fox card, can I spend a bird card instead? And the other way round?
questions.expected_verdict: Yes — birds are wild and can be treated as any suit, even when you must discard or spend a specific suit. But a non-bird card can never be treated as a bird.
questions.notes: Reworded: the rulebook talks about spending, not discarding.
questions.expected_quote: you can always treat a bird card as a mouse, fox, or rabbit card

questions.question: As the Woodland Alliance, does spreading sympathy into a clearing with 3 Marquise warriors cost the normal amount?
questions.expected_verdict: No: Martial Law — if another player has three or more warriors there, it costs one more supporter.
questions.notes: Verified. PDF text on this page is scrambled by layout: good fuzzy-matching test.
questions.expected_quote: Martial Law

questions.question: wait can my cats leave a spot where we're tied with the birds
questions.expected_verdict: Only if you rule the clearing you move to: on a tie no one rules your starting clearing (for you), so it can't be the one that lets you move. Branch: if you are the Eyrie, you rule tied clearings (Lords of the Forest).
questions.expected_quote: To move, you must rule the clearing you are moving from or moving to
questions.notes: Verified. Combines the move rule, the tie rule and the Eyrie exception.

questions.question: I'm the first to take from the center. Do I have to take the first-player tile, and does it cost me anything?
questions.expected_verdict: Yes: you must take it, place it on the leftmost free space of your floor line (it counts as a floor tile, so it costs points), and you start the next round.
questions.notes: Verified. "counts as a normal tile there" is on p.5.
questions.expected_quote: places it on the leftmost space of her floor line

questions.question: Can I put blue tiles in my third pattern line if there's already a blue tile in the third row of my wall?
questions.expected_verdict: No. You cannot place tiles of a color in a pattern line whose wall row already has that color.
questions.expected_quote: You are not allowed to place tiles of a certain color in a pattern line whose corresponding line of your wall already holds a tile of that color

questions.question: Can I dump my tiles straight onto the floor line even though a pattern line could take them?
questions.expected_verdict: Yes. Tiles you cannot or do not want to place in a pattern line go to the floor line (and score its penalty).
questions.source: BGA forum thread https://forum.boardgamearena.com/viewtopic.php?p=142923 and Azul FAQ topic (https://rulespal.com/azul/faq Q9)
questions.expected_quote: cannot or do not want to place according to the rules

questions.question: I'm placing a tile on my wall that has 2 tiles directly to its left and 1 tile directly above it. How many points is it worth?
questions.expected_verdict: 5 points: 3 for the horizontal line (including the new tile) plus 2 for the vertical line.
questions.source: own (rulebook scoring example is a diagram)
questions.notes: Verified. Text + scoring diagram on p.5; expected_box still to draw.
questions.expected_quote: count all these linked tiles (including the newly placed one) and gain that many points

questions.question: End of game: what's a completed column worth compared to a completed row and all five of one color?
questions.expected_verdict: Row: 2 points each. Column: 7 points each. All 5 tiles of one color: 10 points each.
questions.expected_quote: Gain 7 points for each complete vertical line

questions.question: I've got 8 tiles that have to go on my floor line. What's the penalty?
questions.expected_verdict: The floor line has 7 spaces (−1, −1, −2, −2, −2, −3, −3) for a maximum of −14; the 8th tile goes to the box lid with no extra penalty.
questions.notes: Verified. The -1/-1/-2/-2/-2/-3/-3 values exist ONLY in the board illustration, not in the text: the real figure test.
questions.expected_quote: return any further fallen tiles to the lid of the game box

questions.question: can i throw red on the line that's already got blue on it
questions.expected_verdict: No. If a pattern line already holds tiles, you may only add tiles of the same color.
questions.expected_quote: If the pattern line already holds tiles, you may only add tiles of the same color to it

questions.question: I still have an agent left. Can I take my reveal turn now anyway?
questions.expected_verdict: Yes. Agent turns are optional; you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents, and then you take no more turns this round.
questions.source: Dire Wolf rules/FAQ topics (https://www.direwolfdigital.com/assets/dune/DUNE_IMPERIUM_Rules_2020_10_26.pdf); wording ours
questions.expected_quote: you can take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents

questions.question: Two of us tie for the highest strength in combat. Who gets the first-place reward?
questions.expected_verdict: Nobody: tied players for first each get the second-place reward instead (and if tied for second, they get third-place reward).
questions.expected_quote: When players tie for first place, no one wins the Conflict

questions.question: I have 6 swords in my reveal but no troops in the conflict. Do the swords count?
questions.expected_verdict: No. If you have no units in the Conflict your strength is 0, regardless of swords.
questions.expected_quote: You must have at least one troop in the Conflict to have any strength

questions.question: I send an agent to a combat space. How many troops can I put into the conflict?
questions.expected_verdict: Any troops you recruited this turn, plus up to 2 troops from your garrison.
questions.expected_quote: plus up to two more troops from your garrison

questions.question: Someone just hit 10 points mid-round. Does the game end right now?
questions.expected_verdict: No. The game ends at the end of that round (after combat and Makers), when a player has 10+ VP or the Conflict deck is empty; Endgame Intrigue cards are then played.
questions.expected_quote: if any player has reached 10 or more Victory Points

questions.question: im out of agents, can i still do the kwisatz thing
questions.expected_verdict: Yes. Kwisatz Haderach lets you take an Agent turn even with no Agents left in your supply, by sending an Agent that is already on a board space (it can even go back to the same space).
questions.expected_quote: take an Agent turn even if you have no Agents left in your supply

questions.question: ok so ties in the fight, me and jo both at 8, who gets the good stuff
questions.expected_verdict: Neither gets first place: tied players for first each receive the second reward (in a 4-player game the others still compete for the third).
questions.expected_quote: The tied players each receive the second reward
questions.notes: Sloppy rephrasing of du-02: checks that wording does not change the answer.
